correctness.rationale: The finite orthonormal polynomial basis and exact incomplete-beta cap eigenvalues yield a simple top eigenvalue with binomial-tail gaps. Direct shape differentiation and the exact simple-eigenvalue second-order formula give each Hessian mode coefficient. Strictly increasing reverse binomial ratios prove strict multiplier ordering; direct algebra yields the second-harmonic constant. Binomial-to-Poisson convergence and dominated convergence establish the limit. The embedded checker independently evaluates finite matrices for 163 deterministic tests; it is corroboration, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The finite-dimensional coherent-state Faber–Krahn problem has natural equality caps and translation symmetries, so its sharp local angular stability spectrum is a motivated structural invariant. The result explicitly identifies the nullspace and the weakest nonzero Fourier mode, sharp for every finite representation degree and cap area, whereas global optimization and qualitative/nonsharp stability do not provide this quantitative directional information. The finite-spin spectral plateau at angular indices above N and its Gaussian limit help distinguish finite representation effects.
